title: Architecture & Standards: API, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance targets, and our key ADRs. It is intended as the canonical reference for engineers making design decisions that affect runtime behavior, service contracts, operational readiness, and customer-facing SLAs.

Scope
- Applies to all production services and customer-facing APIs (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private control plane).
- Includes service design, CI/CD, IaC, monitoring, and release procedures.
- Excludes low-risk experimental prototypes (see exceptions).

Principles
1. Developer-first: clear, discoverable, and consistent APIs.
2. Production-ready by default: instrumentation, testing, and rollback plans required for any change to runtime code.
3. Observable and measurable: every service must emit standard metrics, traces, and structured logs.
4. Performance-aware by design: trades between latency, throughput, and cost must be explicit and documented.

1) API Standards
- Versioning & Compatibility:
  - Use semantic versioning for public API surfaces (v1, v2). Minor backwards-compatible additions permitted; breaking changes require a new major version and migration plan.
  - Path-based versioning: /v1/generate, /v2/chat.
- Contract & Schema:
  - All request/response payloads must have JSON Schema documentation in the service repo under /api/schemas.
  - Response envelopes must include: request_id, server_time_ms, model_version, and optionally model_variant.
- Error Handling:
  - Use top-level error object: {"error": {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional}}.
  - Standard error codes (string): invalid_request, unauthorized, rate_limited, backend_unavailable, model_error, timeout.
  - HTTP statuses: 4xx for client errors, 429 for rate limits, 5xx for server errors/timeouts.
- Pagination & Limits:
  - Cursor-based pagination for list endpoints.
  - Default page_size <= 100; maximum page_size = 1000 with explicit tenant-level limits.
- Authentication & Authorization:
  - All APIs require API keys with RBAC. Private deployments may use mTLS + API keys.
- Example endpoint spec (short):
  - POST /v1/generate
    - Body schema: {"model": "string", "input": "string|array", "max_tokens": "integer", "temperature": "number"}
    - Successful response: {"request_id":"string","outputs": [...], "model_version":"string"}

2) Coding Standards
- Languages: Primary backend languages are Go (services/runtime control plane) and Python (data pipelines, evals tooling). C++/CUDA for runtime kernel components.
- Style & Linting:
  - Go: gofmt + golangci-lint with error-level rules enabled.
  - Python: black + ruff + mypy (strictness: error on unresolved types for public packages).
- Testing:
  - Unit tests: >80% coverage for public packages. Use table-driven tests in Go.
  - Integration tests: every service must include at least one end-to-end CI job that runs against a disposable test environment.
  - Performance/regression tests included in PRs that touch runtime or model-serving code paths.
- Dependency policy:
  - Avoid unpinned transitive dependencies for production services. Dependabot or equivalent must be enabled.

3) Infrastructure Standards
- IaC & Environments:
  - Use Terraform for cloud infra; modules must be published in the org registry.
  - Environments: dev, staging, prod. Parity requirement: staging should match prod networking and auth controls where feasible.
- Networking & Security:
  - All services expose only necessary ports; default deny network policy in Kubernetes namespaces.
  - Secrets must be stored in KMS-backed secret stores (AWS Secrets Manager or Vault for Private deployments).
- Capacity & Scaling:
  - Autoscaling policies must be defined in Terraform (target CPU/queue-based scaling for control plane; custom metrics for runtime e.g., requests_per_gpu).
- Disaster Recovery:
  - Backup cadence: daily snapshots for critical stateful stores, 30-day retention default. Runbook for restore located at /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/dr-restore.

4) Model-Serving Standards
- Model Packaging:
  - Models must be stored in an immutable artifact repository with manifest (model-name, version, framework, tokenizer, sizes, supported-sequence-length).
  - Use hashed URIs for artifact immutability (e.g., s3://models/<name>/v1/<sha256>.tar.gz).
- Quantization & Variants:
  - Recommended default: FP16 for GPU-hosted; INT8/4-bit quantization allowed with documented quality impact and recommended eval prompts.
  - Quantization profiles live under /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles and must include eval results and token-level quality regressions.
- KV Cache & Prefetch:
  - Services that maintain KV cache must expose cache hit/miss metrics and TTLs. Default per-request KV cache TTL = 5 minutes for session-prefetch.
- Rollouts & Canary:
  - New model versions must follow rollout plan: internal canary -> 5% external traffic -> 25% -> 100% with 24-hour observation windows.
  - Automatic rollback triggers: increase in error_rate > 2x baseline or tail_latency (p99) increases > 30% during rollout window.

5) Observability Standards
- Metrics (required):
  | metric_name | description | unit | SLO/alert threshold |
  |-------------|-------------|------|---------------------|
  | api.request.count | total requests | count | n/a |
  | api.request.latency.p50 | median latency | ms | SLOs defined below |
  | api.request.latency.p95 | 95th percentile latency | ms | alert if > target + 20% |
  | api.request.latency.p99 | 99th percentile tail latency | ms | critical alert if > target + 50% |
  | model.kv_cache.hit_rate | KV cache hit rate | ratio | alert if < 60% |
  | gpu.utilization | GPU utilization | percent | alert if > 95% sustained 10m |
  | infra.disk.utilization | disk percent | percent | alert if > 80% |
- Tracing & Logs:
  - Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry. All external-facing requests must propagate request_id and trace context.
  - Logs must be structured JSON with fields: timestamp, level, service, request_id, span_id, message, extras.
- Dashboards & Alerts:
  - Every service must have a standard Health dashboard (latency, error_rate, QPS, resource usage) and an Oncall runbook link.
  - Pager thresholds: use alert burn windows to reduce noise (e.g., 10m sustained before paged for infra perf alerts).

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarks
- SLOs (example canonical SLOs for public hosted generation API):
  | SLO name | Target | Window | Notes |
  |----------|--------|--------|-------|
  | availability | 99.95% | 30d | measured at API gateway level |
  | latency.p95 | <= 300ms | 30d | for small models (<= 7B) typical; larger models have relaxed targets documented per model profile |
  | latency.p99 | <= 800ms | 30d | host-level p99 target for small models |
  | error_rate | <= 0.1% | 30d | excludes client errors and expected model rejections |
- Benchmarking Process:
  1. Define workload profile (seq length, batch size, token generation length).
  2. Use the benchmarking harness in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
  3. Capture P50/P95/P99, GPU utilization, and end-to-end cost per token. Store run artifacts and perf profiles in the benchmarks bucket.
- Performance Regression Policy:
  - Any PR that increases p95 latency by >10% on the canonical benchmark must include mitigation or explicit approval from runtime team.

7) Decision Records (ADRs) Summary
- ADR-2024-001: API Versioning Strategy — Adopted path-based semver (v1/) and compatibility guarantees for minor changes.
- ADR-2025-007: Model Quantization Defaults — Default FP16 on GPUs; allow INT8/4-bit with documented evals.
- ADR-2025-012: Observability Stack — Adopt OpenTelemetry, Prometheus for metrics, and Loki/ELK for logs.
- ADR-2026-002: Rollout & Canary Policy — Standardized staged rollouts with automated rollback triggers.

Each ADR is stored in /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr/ and includes motivation, alternatives considered, and rollout/rollback criteria.

Governance & Process
- Ownership:
  - Architecture & Standards steward: Aisha Patel (architecture-and-standards).
  - Runtime/Serving: Eng-serving-runtime team owner: Marcus Lee.
  - Observability platform: Eng-platform owner: Elena Garcia.
- Change process:
  1. Raise proposed change as an ADR in the ADR folder with an initial draft.
  2. Request reviewers (minimum two) and allow 7 business days for feedback.
  3. If the ADR impacts SLOs or infra costs, schedule a review with eng-sre and finance.
  4. Upon approval, publish and schedule rollout/migration with stakeholders.

Appendix: Practical examples and templates
- Example response envelope (JSON Schema):
  {
    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
    "title": "GenerateResponse",
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["request_id","outputs","model_version"],
    "properties": {
      "request_id": {"type":"string"},
      "outputs": {"type":"array"},
      "model_version": {"type":"string"},
      "server_time_ms": {"type":"integer"}
    }
  }
- Runbook links:
  - Incident response: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
  - DR restore: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/dr-restore

Questions / Feedback
- For clarifications or proposed exceptions, open an ADR draft and tag @aisha.patel and the relevant owner team.
